In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CEP of χ and η mesons in the central rapidity region is well understood and can be used as an excellent testing ground for QCD.
the CEP of quarkonia is an important process for studying QCD in the nonperturbative region.

the experimental data on CEP of heavy vector mesons are consistent with the predictions of the non-relativistic QCD factorization theorem and the color singlet model for the production of heavy quarkonium states, with the possible exception of the J /ψ data at the Tevatrons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CEP of χ and η mesons at RHIC, Tevatron and LHC energies is dominated by the gluonic component and the color singlet component of the wavefunction is negligible.
the CEP processes are very sensitive to the details of the gluon distribution in the proton and to the gluon propagator.

we have found that the CEP of charmonium (χc and ηc) is very sensitive to the gluonic content of the proton and that the CEP cross sections for charmonium are in good agreement with experimental data from Fermilab and RHIC.

the LHC is the best machine to study the CEP processes.
